core_obligations: Part (1) (proof lines 2256-2266): the composition of two etale morphisms into the space is etale because etaleness into the space is defined by base change to schemes and etale morphisms of schemes are stable under composition.

Part (2) (proof lines 2268-2286): choose a scheme W with a surjective etale morphism to X; base changing the given morphism chi along W gives a morphism between schemes etale over W, which is therefore etale; since the two vertical arrows in the resulting commutative square are surjective and etale, descent of etaleness gives that chi itself is etale.

Part (3) (proof lines 2288-2304): for a scheme W over X consider the pyramid with the base changes of the surjective etale map and the given composites; the base change of that map is again surjective etale and the base change of the composite is etale, so descent of etaleness along the surjective etale map gives the etaleness of the base change of the morphism to W; by definition this means that the morphism into the space is etale.
proof_roadmap: Read the first part off from the definition by base change to schemes and stability under composition.
For the second part, base change along a surjective etale chart and descend etaleness.
For the third part, base change along an arbitrary scheme over the space and use descent again.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves three closure properties of etale morphisms from schemes into an algebraic space: stability under composition, cancellation in a composition, and descent along a surjective etale morphism of schemes (statement lines 2236-2254). The proof (proof lines 2256-2309) reads the first part off from the definition and the stability of etale morphisms under composition, and proves the other two by base changing along a surjective etale chart and applying descent of etaleness. H2: three parts with three inputs, written out in full.
